articles.title: Anthropic's S-1: what its IPO filing teaches marketing, SEO and AI search teams
articles.seoTitle: Anthropic S-1: Lessons for Marketing and AI Search
articles.description: What Anthropic's S-1 teaches marketers: $16.3B first-half revenue, partner fees driving sales spend, free use booked as marketing, citation-aware search.
articles.summary: [[company:anthropic|Anthropic]] filed its S-1 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on October 26, 2026, and has applied to list its Class A stock on Nasdaq as ANT.[^1][^2] The filing shows $16.3 billion of revenue in the first half of 2026 and more than 11,900 customers that each brought in $100,000 or more over 12 months.[^4][^8] Most of the first-half growth in its sales, marketing and partnerships spending came from fees paid to partners, not ads.[^7] This note collects what the filing says that marketing, SEO and AI search teams can use. Statements from the filing are highlighted in green, and each links to its section of the filing.
articles.legend: Green marks what Anthropic's S-1 says. Every green line carries a numbered source that opens the section of the filing it comes from.

stats.label: Revenue in the first half of 2026, up from $1.2B a year earlier
Customers with $100,000 or more of trailing 12-month revenue, up from 950+ a year earlier
First-half 2026 rise in fees paid to channel partners, against $273M more for marketing and advertising

sections.title: Why should marketers read an S-1?

blocks.text: ==An S-1 is the SEC's general form for registering securities under the Securities Act of 1933.==[^1] ==Anthropic filed one on October 26, 2026, for the initial public offering of its Class A stock, which has had no public market until now.==[^1][^2]

==Its annual financial statements are audited: by Grant Thornton for 2023 and 2024, and by Ernst & Young for 2025.==[^10] That makes an S-1 one of the most reliable public accounts a company gives of itself, and it is free to read.

At [[page:/research-and-talks/brightonseo-san-diego-2026|brightonSEO San Diego]] I ([[page:/about|Venkata Pagadala]]) talked about collecting data from sources most search teams never open. Earnings calls are one: on [[article:costco-q4-fy2026-ai-search|Costco's last call]], the CFO named Anthropic among the AI tools where sales now start. An IPO filing is another, and Anthropic has just filed one.

sections.title: The filing in 30 seconds

items: ==Revenue was $41 million in 2023, $386 million in 2024 and $4.6 billion in 2025. In the first half of 2026 it was $16.3 billion, against $1.2 billion a year earlier.==[^4]

==More than 11,900 customers each brought in $100,000 or more in the 12 months to September 30, 2026, up from more than 950 a year earlier.==[^8] ==More than 1,900 brought in $1 million or more, and about 250 brought in $10 million or more.==[^4]

==Net Revenue Retention was about 900% at September 30, 2026.==[^4] By the filing's definition, customers who paid in the third quarter of 2025, leaving out Claude Pro and Max subscribers, brought in about nine times as much in the third quarter of 2026.[^3]
==Adjusted Operating Margin went from minus 159% in the first half of 2025 to plus 10% in the first half of 2026. The GAAP operating loss for the first half of 2026 was $693 million.==[^4]

==Sales, marketing, and partnerships expenses consist mainly of fees paid to channel partners and marketing and advertising costs. In the first half of 2026, fees paid to channel partners rose by $2.7 billion, while marketing and advertising rose by $273 million.==[^7]
==Anthropic has applied to list its Class A stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are listed first among more than 20 underwriters.==[^2]

sections.title: Where does the sales and marketing money go?

blocks.text: ==Anthropic reports one line for sales, marketing, and partnerships. It consists mainly of fees paid to channel partners and marketing and advertising costs, including media and public relations spend.==[^7]

items: ==2024: the line rose by $41 million, and $39 million of that was more marketing and advertising.==[^7]
==2025: fees paid to channel partners rose by $341 million, and marketing and advertising by $170 million.==[^7]

==First half of 2026: the line reached $3.17 billion, up from $120 million a year earlier.==[^4] ==Fees paid to channel partners rose by $2.7 billion, reflecting the growth of the business, and marketing and advertising rose by $273 million, reflecting higher media spend for product launches.==[^7]

blocks.text: ==The notes also group expenses by function. On that basis, sales and marketing cost $3.8 billion in the first half of 2026, against $239 million a year earlier. It includes channel partner costs, marketing and advertising, staff costs, and the compute cost of providing free access to Anthropic's intelligence service.==[^12]

==Much of Claude's diffusion has been organic, and a large portion of growth to date has been self-service.==[^4][^7] ==As adoption moves further into enterprises and regulated industries, Anthropic is investing in direct go-to-market and Applied AI teams and in partnerships.==[^7]

==Claude is available on all three major cloud platforms: AWS, Google Cloud Platform and Microsoft Azure. Anthropic keeps a direct contract with each customer and pays the cloud provider a fee.==[^4] ==Sales through cloud marketplaces were about 11% of revenue in 2023, 32% in 2024, 47% in 2025 and 48% in the first half of 2026.==[^5]

==Customers can also adopt Claude through systems integrators such as Accenture, Deloitte, KPMG and PwC, and data platforms such as Salesforce and Snowflake. Anthropic recently launched Ode with Anthropic, an AI services company formed with leading private equity firms to bring Claude's capabilities to mid-sized companies.==[^4]

The growth plan lists the same levers: ==grow the direct go-to-market and Applied AI teams, deepen cloud distribution partnerships, invest in brand and marketing, and expand the international presence.==[^4]

sections.title: How does Anthropic describe its funnel and its brand?

blocks.text: ==Claude.ai, the flagship conversational product, is the broadest entry point to Claude. The filing says it delivers top-of-funnel demand generation for enterprise adoption.==[^8] ==In September 2026, Anthropic began merging Claude Cowork and Claude.ai into one application.==[^8]

==A customer's journey often begins with a single use case, then expands across departments, applications and workflows.==[^8] ==In the third quarter of 2026, Claude Enterprise users who did not use Claude Code spent less than $75 a month on average. The top 5% of Claude Enterprise users who used Claude Code spent about 20 times that.==[^8]

==Claude Cowork, released as a research preview in January 2026, had by September 30, 2026 been adopted faster than Claude Code was at the same point after its own research preview in February 2025.==[^4]

==Over 50% of the Fortune 500 and over 30% of the Global 2000 were customers with $100,000 or more of trailing 12-month revenue at September 30, 2026. For the publicly traded Fortune 500 customers, Anthropic's revenue averaged less than 0.1% of their total expenses in the third quarter.==[^7]

==The filing lists what promoting its brand depends on: reliable, high-quality and responsible products; sales and marketing, including industry events and key media coverage; customers' testimonials, use cases and word of mouth; security and reliability; the actions of management; and differentiation, including monetization strategies that differ from those of certain competitors.==[^5]

==It also names a cost of free users: if supporting them costs more than the value of their eventual conversion and of benefits such as network effects and word-of-mouth referrals, results could suffer.==[^5]

sections.title: What does the filing say about AI search and the open web?

blocks.text: ==Web Search is a native tool that gives Claude real-time web information, enabling grounded, citation-aware responses in production applications. Claude.ai includes web search too.==[^8]

==The filing defines prompt injection as an adversarial technique in which malicious instructions are embedded in content an AI model is asked to process, such as websites, documents or tool outputs.==[^3] ==It lists prompt injection among the AI-specific threats to its systems.==[^5]
==It defines hallucinations as outputs in which a model generates factually incorrect or fabricated information with apparent confidence, and it discloses them as a risk.==[^3][^5]

==MCP, the Model Context Protocol, is an open standard Anthropic introduced in November 2024 and donated to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation in December 2025. It defines a universal interface through which Claude and other AI tools can connect to enterprise data sources, tools and workflows.==[^8]

Web content is also in court. ==The filing says its data collection has been the subject of litigation alleging that its scraping, web crawling and other techniques to collect data violate the law.==[^5] ==Reddit sued in June 2025, alleging that Anthropic improperly accessed posts on its platform, and in September 2026 the court narrowed the case to breach of contract, interference with contract and unfair competition.==[^5][^11] ==In October 2026, a group of Canadian news publishers alleged that Anthropic copied content from their websites, breached the sites' terms of service and circumvented technological protection measures. Anthropic disputes the allegations in both cases.==[^11]

sections.title: Which agent terms does the filing define?

blocks.text: Buyers will learn these words from filings like this one. Using the same definitions on your own pages makes them easier for people and assistants to match.

items: ==Agent loop: the cycle in which an AI agent receives a task, takes an action, observes the result and decides its next step, repeating until the task is complete.==[^3]

==Agentic AI: AI systems that, with varying degrees of autonomy, can plan, determine and sequence actions and execute them to accomplish defined objectives, including through interaction with external tools, services, datasets and environments on behalf of a user.==[^3]

==Context window: the maximum amount of text, code or other content, measured in tokens, that a model can process in one request, including instructions, prior conversation history, user input and the model's output.==[^3]
==Tokens: the numeric units into which a model converts the data it processes, including text, images, audio and video. They can correspond to words, subwords, characters or bytes.==[^3]
==Prosumers: individual users who subscribe to AI tools to perform knowledge work.==[^3]
==Closing the loop: a development cycle in which successive versions of an AI model assist in building the next, with the goal of compounding capability gains over time.==[^3]
==Virtual Collaborators: AI designed to be embedded where work gets done.==[^4]
==Agent Skills: a modular framework that lets organizations encode repeatable tasks, workflows and domain expertise into reusable packages, or skills, that Claude loads on demand.==[^8]

sections.title: What does the filing say about benchmarks and metrics?

blocks.text: ==The filing warns that the industry benchmarks commonly used to test AI models may not reflect real-world performance or utility, and that models scoring well may not meet customer expectations in production.==[^5]

==Certain success rates and similar performance metrics for Claude in the prospectus come from internal benchmarks built on tasks, data sets and evaluation criteria Anthropic selects. Others using different tasks, data, criteria or computing environments may not be able to replicate them.==[^5]

==Operating metrics such as Run-Rate Revenue, Net Revenue Retention and customer counts come from internal systems and have not been independently verified by third parties.==[^5] ==The Run-Rate Revenue figure itself is left blank in this version of the filing.==[^8]

sections.title: What happened when the cost per task fell?

blocks.text: ==Most revenue is pay-for-intelligence: customers pay for usage, metered in tokens and priced by the model they choose. In the first half of 2026, consumption-based revenue was $13.1 billion, 80% of the total, and subscription revenue was $3.2 billion, 20%.==[^7]

==Opus 4.5 launched in November 2025 with more capability and a lower price and cost per task than Opus 4.1. Quarter-over-quarter revenue growth then rose from 48% in the fourth quarter of 2025 to 132% in the first quarter of 2026. The filing credits several factors: lower prices and better capability that unlocked new use cases, new products, and wider adoption.==[^8]

==With the release of Claude Fable 5.1 in September 2026, Anthropic cut the cost of typical workloads by about 25% against Fable 5, and by up to 45% for complex coding and highly agentic tasks. With Opus 5.5, released the same month, it cut customers' cost per task by about 40% against Opus 5. In each case the cut combined a lower price and improved efficiency.==[^8]
==Revenue grew 1,368% year over year in the second quarter of 2026, while compute and infrastructure expenses grew 300%.==[^4]

sections.title: How does Anthropic size its market?

blocks.text: ==Anthropic says the work that knowledge workers perform was worth more than $40 trillion globally in 2025.==[^4] ==That figure is its own estimate of global knowledge workers' wages, built from U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics wage data, International Labor Organization data on labor income as a share of GDP, and 2025 global GDP.==[^6]
==It also cites IDC's estimate that investment in AI solutions and services will yield a cumulative global economic impact of $22.5 trillion by 2031.==[^4]
Read the $40 trillion as the value of the work AI could help with, measured in wages. It is not a revenue forecast or a market size.

sections.title: What should marketing, SEO and AI search teams take from this?

blocks.text: This part is my read, not Anthropic's words.

items: Distribution beat advertising. In the first half of 2026, fees to channel partners rose about ten times as much as marketing and advertising did, and about 48% of revenue came through cloud marketplaces. For an AI product, the marketplace listing and the integrator network are a major channel.

Organic and self-service growth came first. The filing says much of Claude's diffusion was organic, and it calls its own app demand generation for enterprise. If you market an AI product, the free and prosumer experience is the campaign, and expansion grows from one use case.
Free use is a marketing cost. The notes count the compute cost of free access as sales and marketing, so budget a free tier as acquisition, not as a giveaway.

The brand drivers the filing lists are also the sources AI answers lean on: media coverage, events, testimonials, use cases and word of mouth. Publish named, dated use cases and earn coverage before you buy reach.
To be cited, be fetchable. Claude's web search is built for citation-aware answers, and an agent cannot cite a page it cannot fetch and read. Serve real HTML, keep facts current, and date them.
Never hide instructions for AI in your pages. The filing defines that as prompt injection, an attack it defends against. It is not a GEO tactic.
Hallucinations are a disclosed risk. Keep one clean, sourced page of facts about your company, and check what assistants say about you every month.
Benchmarks are not proof: the company warns investors that benchmark scores may not reflect real-world results. Sell outcomes on the buyer's own tasks.

Re-cost agent work at every model release. Anthropic's September 2026 releases cut customer costs by about 25% to 40%, and up to 45% on complex agentic work, through lower prices and better efficiency. A workflow that is too expensive today may pay next quarter.
Size the market by the work, not the software budget. Anthropic frames its opportunity as the value of knowledge work, so the buyer compares it with payroll, not with other software.

Watch how AI companies collect web content. The filing says its scraping and web crawling have drawn lawsuits, and the Canadian publishers allege breach of website terms and circumvention of technological protection measures. Make sure your own terms and access rules say what you mean.
Read filings. An S-1's risk factors are a free map of what a market leader worries about, written for regulators and investors.

sections.title: Who controls Anthropic after the IPO?

blocks.text: ==Anthropic is a Delaware public benefit corporation. Its public benefit purpose is the responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity.==[^2]

==A Long-Term Benefit Trust, intended to operate as an independent body of financially disinterested trustees, holds Class T stock. Through it, the trust generally has the authority to elect and remove the Class T directors, who will make up a majority of the board. Class T stock has no economic rights.==[^2]

==Just before the offering, a Founder LLC whose members are the seven co-founders will receive a single share of Class F stock. It carries 50.1% of the vote on matters put to stockholders generally, including electing the directors other than the Class T directors, and has no economic rights.==[^2][^4]

==Anthropic contributed 846,840,960 Class N shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund: 5% of its fully diluted shares as of June 30, 2026, assuming full conversion of the Amazon Notes. The board may, at its discretion, issue up to 2% more of the then-outstanding shares each time the share price rises 50% above the previous milestone, starting from the IPO price.==[^4] ==Each co-founder has pledged to dedicate 80% of their personal equity in Anthropic to philanthropic causes.==[^4] ==The filing describes these pledges as voluntary and revocable, not legally binding.==[^5]
==Under Nasdaq's governance rules, Anthropic is considered a controlled company.==[^2]

sections.title: Which other risks should marketers know about?

items: ==In April 2026, Anthropic released its Mythos model only as a gated research preview through Project Glasswing, for select organizations' cybersecurity work, because of its advanced ability to find software vulnerabilities.==[^5]

==In June 2026, the U.S. Department of Commerce imposed worldwide export restrictions on the Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models. Anthropic disabled them for all customers until the restrictions were lifted, after it updated its safeguards.==[^5]

==In September 2025, Anthropic agreed to settle the Bartz copyright class action for $1.5 billion, and the court approved the settlement in July 2026. Music publishers have sued over song lyrics.==[^5] ==La Presse, a Quebec news publisher, sued in July 2026.==[^11]
==Sales through cloud marketplaces made up 58% of net accounts receivable at June 30, 2026.==[^5]

sections.title: Who is named in the filing?

blocks.text: ==[[person:dario-amodei]] is Chief Executive Officer and a co-founder, and [[person:daniela-amodei]] is President, a co-founder and Chairperson. [[person:krishna-rao]] has been Chief Financial Officer since April 2024.==[^9]
==The non-employee directors are Reed Hastings, Christopher Liddell, Vas Narasimhan and Yasmin Razavi.==[^9]

==Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are listed first among the underwriters, followed by J.P. Morgan, Citigroup, Barclays, Wells Fargo Securities, BofA Securities, Deutsche Bank Securities, RBC Capital Markets and UBS Investment Bank, among others.==[^2]
==Grant Thornton audited the 2023 and 2024 financial statements, and Ernst & Young the 2025 statements.==[^10]

articles.title: Costco's Q4 FY2026 earnings call: what the CFO said about AI search
articles.seoTitle: Costco Q4 FY2026 Earnings Call: What It Said About AI
articles.description: Costco's CFO said AI search traffic grew triple digits for a second quarter and converts best of any source. Every AI statement from the call, with sources.
articles.summary: Costco reported its fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 on September 24, 2026. On the call, CFO [[person:gary-millerchip]] said traffic from AI search grew triple digits for the second quarter in a row and converts better than any other traffic to costco.com. This note collects every AI and digital statement from the call, highlighted in green, each with its source.
articles.legend: Green marks what Costco said about AI and digital. Every line carries a numbered source.

sections.title: Why read an earnings call?

blocks.text: At [[page:/research-and-talks/brightonseo-san-diego-2026|brightonSEO San Diego]] I ([[page:/about|Venkata Pagadala]]) talked about collecting data from sources most search teams never open, and earnings calls were one of them. A call is dated, on the record, and every statement has a name attached: here, Costco's CEO [[person:ron-vachris]] and CFO [[person:gary-millerchip]]. That makes it primary evidence of how AI is changing shopping, from the company that sees the numbers.

items: The slides: [[url:https://speakerdeck.com/venkatapagadala1/industrial-context-graphs?slide=22|Industrial context graphs]] on Speaker Deck, opening at slide 22.
The write-up: [[url:https://previsible.com/brightonseo/demand-research-beyond-keywords/|User First, Algorithm Second: Researching Demand Beyond Search Volume]] on Previsible.

sections.title: The call in 30 seconds

items: ==Traffic to costco.com from AI search grew triple digits for the second quarter in a row, and it converts better than any other source of traffic.==[^2]
==Sales that start in AI tools also grew triple digits, from a low base. The CFO named Gemini, Anthropic and OpenAI.==[^2]
==Costco does no paid digital advertising, so the CFO sees AI as a neutral place where its value can show up on its own merits.==[^2]
==The work behind it is data: Costco's teams are cleaning up product data and product pages for the AI models.==[^2]
==Digitally enabled comparable sales rose 19.5% in the quarter==, on net sales of $93.9 billion, up 11.2%.[^1]

sections.title: What did Costco say about AI search?

blocks.text: ==Traffic to Costco's site from AI search grew at a triple-digit rate for the second consecutive quarter, and it still has the highest conversion rate of all traffic to the site.==[^2] ==The channel is young: the CFO said it is growing from a low base compared with Costco's other channels, while AI keeps gaining influence on how members search for products.==[^2]

==Sales that start in AI search are led by appliances and consumer electronics, the same categories that lead Costco's e-commerce overall.==[^2] ==The Costco membership itself is among the top items that AI searches lead to, which the CFO read as a sign of how members value it.==[^2]

sections.title: Is this agentic commerce yet?

blocks.text: Rupesh Parikh of Oppenheimer asked how Costco is positioned for agentic commerce.[^2] ==The CFO's answer: not agentic commerce at the moment. What Costco sees is members using AI as a tool to search for products as they plan what to buy.==[^2]
==Sales that originate from searches on the large language models are growing at triple-digit rates. He named the tools: Gemini, Anthropic and OpenAI.==[^2]

==Costco does no paid digital advertising. The CFO described AI as a neutral environment where Costco's value and quality can show up transparently, helped by a curated range of items its buyers vet personally.==[^2]
==The work behind it: Costco's teams are working with the large language models on how to clean up and update its product data and product pages, so its value keeps showing up accurately.==[^2]

sections.title: What else moved in digital?

items: ==Digitally enabled comparable sales grew 19.5% in the quarter (19.8% excluding currency) and 20.9% for the full year.==[^1]
==Digitally enabled sales, including third-party delivery, exceeded $33 billion for the year, up more than 20%.==[^2]
==Total site and app traffic was up 30%.==[^2]
==Personalization, through product placements and emails, grew sales at a triple-digit rate, and 10% of costco.com orders now include a personalized item.==[^2]
==Costco is discontinuing Costco Next, its extended marketplace, and moving its most popular items and brands into the main app and website.==[^2]

sections.title: What should search and AI teams take from this?

blocks.text: This part is my read, not Costco's words.

items: AI answers are now a sales channel that a retailer of Costco's size measures: it tracks the traffic, the conversion rate and the products sold.
The lever Costco named is product data and product pages. That is work search teams already own.
A brand with no paid digital ads can still win in AI answers, if its value is visible in its own data.
Earnings calls are free, dated and attributable. Read them for every company in your market, and log what they say about AI each quarter.

sections.title: What were the finance numbers?

items.label: Q4 comparable sales; 6.7% excluding gas and currency
Q4 earnings per diluted share, including a one-time $0.15 from tariff refunds
Renewal rate in the US and Canada; 89.8% worldwide

items: Excluding the one-time tariff benefit, net income grew 12.3% and earnings per share 12.4%.[^2]
Fiscal 2026 net income was $9.226 billion, $20.76 per diluted share.[^1]
Gross margin was 11.02%, down 11 basis points, or up 20 basis points excluding gas. The LIFO charge was $152 million, against $43 million a year earlier.[^2]
SG&A was 8.94% of sales, 27 basis points better than a year ago. The tax rate was 25.2%.[^2]
Capital spending was $2.21 billion in Q4 and $6.4 billion for fiscal 2026, with about $7.5 billion planned for fiscal 2027.[^2]
Q4 was the last quarter to benefit from the membership fee increase.[^2]

sections.title: What else did Costco cover on the call?

items: Warehouses: 12 opened in Q4, 10 of them new US buildings, and 28 in fiscal 2026, three of them relocations, for 939 in total.[^1][^2] Costco plans 33 openings in fiscal 2027, five of them relocations, including 4 in Europe, 5 in Canada and 1 in Mexico, and new US markets such as Buffalo, New York and Lawrence, Kansas.[^2]
Gas: a record year. The share of US member households buying gas reached an all-time high, and Costco estimates it saved members over $3.2 billion.[^2]
Pharmacy: sales grew nearly 20%, helped by GLP-1 and fertility programs, and Costco has a new partnership with SCAN to develop Medicare Advantage benefits.[^2]
Travel: Costco sent over 750,000 members on cruises, up 16%.[^2]
Members: the member base under 40 has grown nearly 60% since COVID and is now more than a quarter of all members.[^2]

Tariff refunds: Costco received $184 million in Q4, $174 million in refunds plus $10 million in interest, a little more than a third of what it expects.[^2] Part of the refunds was reinvested in increased member value.[^1]

Merchandise: non-foods comparable sales grew mid- to high-single digits, led by gold and jewelry and home furnishings. Fresh grew mid-single digits, led by bakery and meat, with in-house pastries up over 100%.[^2]
Kirkland Signature price cuts: walnuts from $13.79 to $9.99, and Colombian whole bean coffee from $21.99 to $19.99.[^2]
Ancillary businesses: comparable sales up in the high 20s, with gas up in the mid-30s. Inflation stayed in the low single digits.[^2]
Next update: September sales results on October 7, 2026.[^2]
